Determine if $\mathbf{b} \in \textrm{Col}(B).$ 
In the affirmative case, find the values of $x_1$ and $x_2,$ where $x_1$ and $x_2$ are the real numbers such that $\mathbf{b}=x_1\mathbf{b}_1+x_2\mathbf{b}_2,$ and $\mathbf{b}_1,$ $\mathbf{b}_2$ are the respective columns of $B.$

![](images/a6/a65747aa11107acc9a05df83473ed0208c23818953b16771b608ec4f572dc7ca.svg)" :question/worked-solution "In order to determine whether $\mathbf{b}$ lies in $\textrm{Col}(B),$ we need to check if the equation $B\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{b}$ is consistent. So, let's find the row echelon form of the augmented matrix $[B \,|\, \mathbf{b}]$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[B\,|\,b] & =[\begin{aligned}5 & -2 & 7 \\ 15 & -6 & 21 \\ 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}5 & -2 & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & ↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}5 & -2 & 7 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we have the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}5{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}=7 \\ {x}_{2}=0 \\ 0=0.\end{aligned}
$$

From the third equation, we get the true statement $0=0.$ So the system is equivalent to the following:

$$
{\begin{aligned}5{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}=7 \\ {x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

From the second equation, we get $x_2=0.$ Substituting into the first equation gives $x_1=\dfrac 7 5.$ 

Since we have a solution, the equation $B\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{b}$ is consistent, which implies that $\mathbf{b}\in\textrm{Col}(B).$

Moreover, there is exactly one solution, so we have exactly one way to write $\mathbf{b}$ as a linear combination of $\mathbf{b}_1$ and $\mathbf{b}_2\mathbin{:}$

![](images/02/027332c5a5bdb14913d297e71bc2ac2ae8f846976c1bc3c0c4c569997dcd5b01.svg)" :question/worked-solution "In order to determine whether $\mathbf{b}$ lies in $\textrm{Col}(C),$ we need to check if the equation $C\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{b}$ is consistent. So, let's find the row echelon form of the augmented matrix $[C \,|\, \mathbf{b}]$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[C\,|\,b] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 4 & 5 \\ -1 & 2 & 0 & -4 \\ 0 & -3 & 1 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 4 & 5 \\ 0 & 3 & 4 & 1 \\ 0 & -3 & 1 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 4 & 5 \\ 0 & 3 & 4 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 5 & 5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we have the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+4{x}_{3}=5 \\ 3{x}_{2}+4{x}_{3}=1 \\ 5{x}_{3}=5.\end{aligned}
$$

From the third equation, we get $x_3=1$. Substituting into the second equation gives 

$$
\begin{aligned}3{x}_{2}+4(1) & =1 \\ 3{x}_{2} & =-3 \\ {x}_{2} & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, from the first equation, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =5-{x}_{2}-4{x}_{3} \\  & =5-(-1)-4(1) \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Since we have a solution, the equation $C\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{b}$ is consistent, which implies that $\mathbf{b}\in\textrm{Col}(C).$ 

Moreover, there is exactly one solution, so we have exactly one way to write $\mathbf{b}$ as a linear combination of $\mathbf{c}_1,$ $\mathbf{c}_2,$ and $\mathbf{c}_3\mathbin{:}$
![](images/4c/4cccd67d5e043d72e0b6949543883e6187d9ef807b7a470146628cbadf7eead7.svg)

Finally, we get $x_1 \cdot x_2 \cdot x_3 = 2 \cdot (-1) \cdot 1 = -2$." :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "question-0a92dafd-51fb-510b-93ec-662d06afe5a3" :question/id #uuid "0a92dafd-51fb-510b-93ec-662d06afe5a3" :question/math-academy-id "q-34503" :question/problem "The matrix $K$ and the vector $b$ are given below. Now, we have the system

$$

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 3 \\ -2 & 10 & -7 \\ 3 & -12 & 10\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 11 \\ -13\end{aligned}]
$$" :question/worked-solution "In order to determine whether $b$ lies in $\text{Col}(A),$ we need to check if the equation $Ax=b$ is consistent. So, let's find the row echelon form of the augmented matrix $[A\,|\,b]$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[A\,|\,b] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 3 & -4 \\ -2 & 10 & -7 & 11 \\ 3 & -12 & 10 & -13\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 3 & -4 \\ 0 & 2 & -1 & 3 \\ 3 & -12 & 10 & -13\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 3 & -4 \\ 0 & 2 & -1 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we have the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-4{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3}=-4 \\ 2{x}_{2}-{x}_{3}=3 \\ {x}_{3}=-1.\end{aligned}
$$

From the third equation, we get ${x}_{3}=-1.$ Substituting it into the second equation gives 

$$
\begin{aligned}2{x}_{2}-(-1) & =3 \\ 2{x}_{2} & =2 \\ {x}_{2} & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, from the first equation, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =-4+4{x}_{2}-3{x}_{3} \\  & =-4+4(1)-3(-1) \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Since we have a solution, the equation $Ax=b$ is consistent, which implies that $b\in \text{Col}(A).$ 

Moreover, there is exactly one solution, so we have exactly one way to write $b$ as a linear combination of ${a}_{1},$ ${a}_{2},$ and ${a}_{3}:$

$$
{{[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 11 \\ -13\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}=3\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ 3\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{1}}+1\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 10 \\ -12\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{2}}+(-1)\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -7 \\ 10\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{3}}
$$

Finally, we get ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=3+1+(-1)=3.$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-eb0ebf0b-554c-514b-a72c-5d817e3dd52a"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-eb0ebf0b-554c-514b-a72c-5d817e3dd52a" :answer-field/id #uuid "eb0ebf0b-554c-514b-a72c-5d817e3dd52a" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/correct "answer-4543a202-3ccc-5eab-b11e-9acd9fffb1d8" :answer-field/choices ["answer-47160327-abda-5117-a3f6-534dafb7314d" "answer-56c7eda1-7b63-555c-9f5f-b736c9f51e0b" "answer-4543a202-3ccc-5eab-b11e-9acd9fffb1d8" "answer-fa79a18c-e454-55de-b1b8-442bf38cb930" "answer-49158a7c-f7b1-5aa2-a277-f0ac8325fc0b"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-47160327-abda-5117-a3f6-534dafb7314d" :answer/id #uuid "47160327-abda-5117-a3f6-534dafb7314d" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "1" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-56c7eda1-7b63-555c-9f5f-b736c9f51e0b" :answer/id #uuid "56c7eda1-7b63-555c-9f5f-b736c9f51e0b" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "2" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-4543a202-3ccc-5eab-b11e-9acd9fffb1d8" :answer/id #uuid "4543a202-3ccc-5eab-b11e-9acd9fffb1d8" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "3" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-fa79a18c-e454-55de-b1b8-442bf38cb930" :answer/id #uuid "fa79a18c-e454-55de-b1b8-442bf38cb930" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "4" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-49158a7c-f7b1-5aa2-a277-f0ac8325fc0b" :answer/id #uuid "49158a7c-f7b1-5aa2-a277-f0ac8325fc0b" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "5" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "question-06040e86-0928-550a-a9a4-3db2bc9e2e31" :question/id #uuid "06040e86-0928-550a-a9a4-3db2bc9e2e31" :question/math-academy-id "q-111046" :question/problem "The matrix $D$ and the vector $b$ are given below.

where we denote its columns by $\color{red}\mathbf{a}_1$ and ${\color{blue}\mathbf{a}_2},$ respectively. The column space of this matrix is given by
![](images/5f/5faad23bc77f821d42223beaca06364e38c7f0ba8a4869cb138e0e923e90b8f7.svg)

Now, suppose we would like to determine whether the vector ![](images/45/45349edee356334c54ad85a6d60757a6a7833a392962086815a2436446e323dc.svg) lies in $\textrm{Col}(A).$ In other words, we need to check if $\mathbf{b} \in \textrm{Span}\{ {\color{red}\mathbf{a}_1}, {\color{blue}\mathbf{a}_2} \}.$ So, we need to determine whether $\mathbf{b}$ can be written as some linear combination of $\color{red}\mathbf{a}_1$ and ${\color{blue}\mathbf{a}_2}\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that the equation above can be written as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}{a}_{1} & {a}_{2}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =b \\ {{[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}{{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{x}} & ={{[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{b}}\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}[A\,|\,b] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 2 \\ 2 & -1 & -3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 2 \\ 0 & -7 & -7\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we have the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}=2 \\ -7{x}_{2}=-7.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second equation, we get $x_2=1.$ Substituting into the first equation, we get $x_1=-1.$

![](images/d9/d9d3fd7384b4375895d234c22c9d81f30358439f7e04ee8db055de9d5d7f1174.svg)
then $\textrm{Col}(A) = \textrm{Span} \{ {\color{black}\mathbf{a}_1}, {\color{black}\mathbf{a}_2}, \ldots, {\color{black}\mathbf{a}_n} \}.$

The column space satisfies the following properties:

- If $A$ is an ${\color{blue}m}\times n$ matrix, then $\textrm{Col}(A)$ is a subspace of $\mathbb{R}^{\color{blue}m}.$ This is because each column has ${\color{blue}m}$ entries.

- $\mathbf{b}\in\textrm{Col}(A)$ if and only if the equation $A\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{b}$ is consistent (has a solution).

- If the equation $A\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{b}$ is inconsistent (has no solution), then $\mathbf{b}\not\in\textrm{Col}(A).$

"5ce2b050-dd59-54b3-bb85-3a4f08ea0365" :topic/math-academy-id 1850} :activity/steps [{:db/id 17592186120686 :step/content {:db/id 17592186121043 :tutorial/content "The **column space** of a matrix $A$ is denoted $\text{Col}(A)$ and is the span of the columns of $A$ (i.e., the set of all possible linear combinations of columns of $A$). For example, consider the matrix

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}]
$$

where we denote its columns by $\color{red}\mathbf{a}_1$ and ${\color{blue}\mathbf{a}_2},$ respectively. The column space of this matrix is given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]
$$

Now, suppose we would like to determine whether the vector $[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3\end{aligned}]$ lies in $\textrm{Col}(A).$ In other words, we need to check if $\mathbf{b} \in \textrm{Span}\{ {\color{red}\mathbf{a}_1}, {\color{blue}\mathbf{a}_2} \}.$ So, we need to determine whether $\mathbf{b}$ can be written as some linear combination of $\color{red}\mathbf{a}_1$ and ${\color{blue}\mathbf{a}_2}\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that the equation above can be written as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}{a}_{1} & {a}_{2}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =b \\ {{[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}{{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{x}} & ={{[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{b}}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the equation is equivalent to $A\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{b}.$ To solve the equation, let's find the row echelon form of the augmented matrix $[A \,|\, \mathbf{b}]$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[A\,|\,b] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 2 \\ 2 & -1 & -3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 2 \\ 0 & -7 & -7\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we have the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}=2 \\ -7{x}_{2}=-7.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second equation, we get $x_2=1.$ Substituting into the first equation, we get $x_1=-1.$

Since we have a solution, the equation $A\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{b}$ is consistent, which implies that $\mathbf{b} \in \textrm{Col}(A).$

Moreover, there is exactly one solution, so we have exactly one way to write $\mathbf{b}$ as a linear combination of $\color{red}\mathbf{a}_1$ and ${\color{blue}\mathbf{a}_2}\mathbin{:}$

$$
[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3\end{aligned}]
$$" :tutorial/id #uuid "f65da145-207a-50c6-b59e-8756d247cc71" :tutorial/math-academy-id 3201 :tutorial/title "Introduction"} :step/id #uuid "e2b22098-86e0-53ea-bbc9-fc31b60b4152" :step/math-academy-id 17489 :step/next {:db/id 17592186120687}} {:db/id 17592186120687 :step/content {:db/id 17592186119816 :knowledge-point/canonical-example {:db/id 17592186119627 :question/id #uuid "244793f6-41c3-5920-9264-bec32cda9c9c" :question/math-academy-id "e-4807"} :knowledge-point/id #uuid "5c8e217c-252d-529f-a810-84787e2ee886" :knowledge-point/key-prerequisites [{:db/id 17592186048321}] :knowledge-point/questions [{:db/id 17592186120319} {:db/id 17592186120345} {:db/id 17592186247188} {:db/id 17592186247189} {:db/id 17592186247191} {:db/id 17592186317423} {:db/id 17592186342186}] :knowledge-point/title "Determining if a Vector is in the Column Space of a Matrix"} :step/id #uuid "415a39b4-7da9-55ac-afde-f8932b3c0813" :step/math-academy-id 17491 :step/next {:db/id 17592186120755}} {:db/id 17592186120688 :step/content {:db/id 17592186121044 :tutorial/content "The column space is defined for matrices of *any* dimensions. In general, if ${\color{black}\mathbf{a}_1}, {\color{black}\mathbf{a}_2}, \ldots, {\color{black}\mathbf{a}_n}$ are the columns of a matrix $A,$ that is to say,

$$
\begin{aligned}| & | &  & | \\ {a}_{1} & {a}_{2} & … & {a}_{n} \\ | & | &  & |\end{aligned}
$$

then $\textrm{Col}(A) = \textrm{Span} \{ {\color{black}\mathbf{a}_1}, {\color{black}\mathbf{a}_2}, \ldots, {\color{black}\mathbf{a}_n} \}.$

The column space satisfies the following properties:

- If $A$ is an ${\color{blue}m}\times n$ matrix, then $\textrm{Col}(A)$ is a subspace of $\mathbb{R}^{\color{blue}m}.$ This is because each column has ${\color{blue}m}$ entries.

- $\mathbf{b}\in\textrm{Col}(A)$ if and only if the equation $A\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{b}$ is consistent (has a solution).

- If the equation $A\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{b}$ is inconsistent (has no solution), then $\mathbf{b}\not\in\textrm{Col}(A).$

These hold for any $m\times n$ matrix, and the matrix does not necessarily have to be square." :tutorial/id #uuid "f33b7df2-b0c3-5b23-b26b-50509cefd3a3" :tutorial/math-academy-id 3203 :tutorial/title
